the day jinho decided
jinho stood outside in the alleyway, nose wrinkled at the smell of the nearby sewer and food rotting from neighbouring restaurants, as he held the cigarette between his fingers. the other hand was stuffed in his pocket, curled around itself to protect from the biting, unforgiving seoul winter that was chilling him down to the bone.

he lifted the fag to his lips, inhaling before exhaling the thin stream of smoke that drifted up and broke apart in the open air. his expression was lost, simply passing time, as the loud bustle of the restaurant behind him continued in his absence. it could wait. jinho's restlessness couldn't.

"fuck," he murmured. reaching for his pocket, he fumbled with his adhd medication bottle. popping one in his mouth and swallowing it dry, he took another hit of the cigarette. how long had jinho been out here? long enough that the tips of his fingers tingled, the cold leaving his nerves pinched.

the faint smell of tobacco wrapped around him. he knew his head chef hated it but he forgot his cologne today, the team in the kitchen was going to have to deal with it.

putting out the cigarette, jinho leaned back against the wall. he may be freezing but he had no desire to retreat back inside, to the shouting, to the barking orders and the demanding team, to the waiting staff who thought they were better than jinho because they weren't trapped in a dead end. no, the waiting staff had ambition. they were college students, this was the job to get them by, to pay for the 7/11 trips and the inexpensive karaoke bars where they sipped their misery away.

for jinho? this was his livelihood. he was alone in seoul now. both his brothers had departed but he stubbornly stayed rooted in the city, having graduated from culinary school and determined to break out of the mold. but equally, he was lost.

his trance was broken when his boss, the head chef, came storming out. donghee was in his fifties and had slaved away at multiple restaurants, begging his way up the ladder to head chef position evidently because his dishes weren't exceptional. the minute donghee had laid eyes on jinho, he had decided he hated him.

donghee held a plate of food that jinho had experimented creating today. he had come ahead of his shift to use the kitchen and try to propose a new menu item - gochujang cream carbonara pasta with king prawns and mussels. it was unlike any other dish the traditional korean restaurant offered but they were slowly dabbling into fusion, especially italian, and jinho wanted to lead the way.

"hyung-nim-" before jinho could continue, donghee smashed the plate on the floor. the sudden sound on the pavement followed by the ceramic shattering made jinho jolt, eyebrow knitting together in genuine bewilderment. "what are you doing?"

the head chef was angered. he reached out to grip the front of jinho's dirty, stained apron, twisting it in his hand to drag him forward. he stumbled forward like a rag doll, the first slither of fear starting to rush through his system. "who exactly do you think you are, jinho?"

the question only further confused him. he knew donghee didn't like him but this reaction was unlike any other treatment he had before. usually, they barely tolerated each other, ignoring each other in the kitchen unless donghee was telling him to prepare something and jinho was shouting back it was ready. it wasn't what jinho desired from his career and it may be a spiralling misery - but he couldn't quit. this was the first restaurant that gave him a job out of culinary school amidst a tough, struggling market, so jinho smoked away the stress and toughened up against donghee's remarks.

but the physical assault was unwarranted. jinho forcefully pushed donghee's hand off him, unable to keep the agitation off his face. "what are you talking about? what have i done?"

"this isn't your restaurant, do you understand? trying to make new dishes, changing recipes, making your own rules. you're merely a sous chef. you're my dog in this place. this is my restaurant. you follow MY orders. don't ever disrespect me again by trying to make your own dish, trying to pitch it to me or the owners. learn your fucking place, jinho. how old are you again?"

the words slowly sank into jinho but didn't fully comprehend to him.

working here meant having no creative liberty. it meant never stepping out of the tightly restricted job description of being a slave, coming in, putting on the apron and working tirelessly at the orders of another miserable, failed chef. what was jinho even doing?

he can't remember the last time he enjoyed cooking. in culinary school, jinho was proud to walk through the doors, to show up to his classes and impress the professors who genuinely wanted to teach. the real world was not the same. the real world was teaching jinho that he was a pawn and he was never going to make it here, not until he submitted to another dozen failed mid-50 men who had a power trip.

glancing down at his now ruined dish, the pasta he curated with time, thought and genuine love for the team, untouched and smeared on the floor only fuelled him. jinho wasn't perfect. he was an addict, a maniac, a loner, he had issues - but he knew his food deserved to be enjoyed by people.

gritting his teeth, jinho just nodded. "it won't happen again."

later when his shift was over that night, jinho hung his apron up. he walked out the door and slipped his key under it. he never intended to return.

he'd create his own destiny, even if it meant leaving the city he loved and moving to where he would be taken seriously. even if that meant reuniting with his brothers.

a day in prison

wake-up call

leo shared his prison cell with a cell-mate that he had barely exchanged more than a few words with. it was pleasant and civil, but leo wasn't interested in making any friends. in order to avoid all and any type of unnecessary contact, leo had trained his body to wake up before the 5:30am wake-up call. his body hadn't relaxed beyond 5am for almost three years and counting now since he came into prison.

as soon as it hit 4:45am, his body tense with anxiety was up. he would hit the showers before anybody had a chance to, letting the lukewarm and then freezing cold water attack his body.

hunger was rare in prison and the food tasted like lead. he'd be the first to come into the breakfast hall, eat quickly, before running off to start his work shift.

work shift

working almost 10-hours a day, leo did the laundry shift. he initially had been assigned to yard clean-up but the heat was scorching and after suffering fainting spells, the doctor finally signed him off. he now worked in the basement of the prison in damp, mouldy conditions, folding prison uniform after uniform for almost 10 hours.

it was close to slave conditions, earning just under a dollar per hour. it went straight to his commissary but he hardly could afford anything, the prices climbing up. on a good day, leo was able to buy himself crackers.

when he was done with his shift, he visited the commissary to buy his regular crackers that he'd eat with cheese at dinnertime. but to his surprise, somebody had deposited $100 - a luxury in prison. he was a millionaire, in prison terms. leo could barely believe what he was hearing and asked the staff member multiple times to confirm.

teary-eyed, he sat in the back of his cell, eating ramen for the first time in 3 years.

winding down

leo was late to dinner but he didn't need to fill his stomach with inedible food, having already enjoyed his favourite 'jin spicy ramen' packet.

he had one friend in prison who, like him, had been caught up with the wrong crowd. they sat together for dinner and played card games together, it was a slither of normalcy in leo's life that he appreciated since he was alone otherwise. once they were done, he retreated back to his room, preparing his body for another 4:45am wake-up call and 10 hour shift.
